items.title: A New Ground Opens: Why Reflection Follows Hearing

items.zh: 已說聞所成地。云何思所成地？當知略說由三種相。一、由自性清淨故；二、由思擇所知故；三、由思擇諸法故。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, the Ground of What Is Attained Through Reflection, the eleventh, part one. The Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing has now been explained. What is the Ground of What Is Attained Through Reflection? Know that, briefly stated, it has three aspects: first, by way of purity of self-nature; second, by way of reflecting on what is cognized; and third, by way of reflecting on the teachings.

items.title: Purity of Self-Nature: Nine Marks of a Mind That Reflects Correctly

items.zh: 云何自性清淨？謂九種相應知。一者、謂如有一、獨處空閑，審諦思惟如其所聞、如所究達諸法道理。二者、遠離一切不思議處，審諦思惟所應思處；三者、能善了知黑說、大說；四者、凡所思惟，唯依於義，不依於文。
items.en: What is purity of self-nature? Know that it has nine marks. First, one dwells alone in solitude and quiet, carefully and truly reflecting on the principles of things exactly as heard and exactly as investigated to their conclusion. Second, one keeps entirely clear of what should not be contemplated, carefully and truly reflecting only on what is fit to be contemplated. Third, one skilfully distinguishes provisional teaching from teaching in its fullest sense. Fourth, whatever one reflects on, one relies solely on the meaning, not on the mere letter.

items.zh: 五者、於法少分，唯生信解；於法少分，以慧觀察。六者、堅固思惟。七者、安住思惟。八者、相續思惟。九者、於所思惟能善究竟，終無中路厭怖退屈。由此九相，名為清淨善淨思惟。
items.en: Fifth, regarding some portion of the Dharma, one simply generates faith and understanding; regarding another portion, one examines it with wisdom. Sixth, one's reflection is firm. Seventh, one's reflection is settled. Eighth, one's reflection is sustained without interruption. Ninth, whatever one reflects on, one carries skilfully through to its conclusion, never growing weary, fearful, or discouraged partway through. By these nine marks, reflection is called pure and rightly purified.

items.title: Reflecting on What Is Cognized Opens: Existing Things and Non-Existing Things

items.zh: 云何思擇所知？謂善思擇所觀察義。何等名為所觀察義？謂於有法了知有相，於非有法了知無相。如是名為所觀察義。
items.en: What is reflecting on what is cognized? It means skilfully reflecting on the object under examination. What is called the object under examination? It means, regarding what genuinely exists, knowing it to have a real mark; and regarding what does not genuinely exist, knowing it to have no real mark. This is called the object under examination.

items.zh: 何等名為所觀有法？當知此法略有五種。一、自相有法，二、共相有法，三、假相有法，四、因相有法，五、果相有法。
items.en: What is called an existing thing under examination? Know that, briefly, it has five kinds: first, a thing existing by its own particular mark; second, a thing existing by a mark shared in common; third, a thing existing by a merely designated mark; fourth, a thing existing by the mark of a cause; and fifth, a thing existing by the mark of a result.

items.zh: 何等名為自相有法？當知此法略有三種。一、勝義相有；二、相狀相有；三、現在相有。勝義相有者，謂諸法中離言說義，出世間智所行境界，非安立相。
items.en: What is called a thing existing by its own particular mark? Know that, briefly, it has three kinds: first, existing in the mark of ultimate meaning; second, existing in the mark of a describable feature; and third, existing in the mark of the present moment. Existing in the mark of ultimate meaning: it refers, among all things, to the meaning beyond verbal description — the object range of transcendent wisdom, a mark not established through conventional designation.

items.title: Two More Kinds of Real Existence: Describable Features and the Present Moment

items.zh: 相狀相有者，謂由四種所觀相狀。一、於是處名可得。二、於是處事可得。三、此名於此事非不決定。謂或迷亂不決定故，或無常不決定故。四、此名於此事無礙隨轉。非或於是處隨轉，或於是處退還。
items.en: Existing in the mark of a describable feature: it means having four observable characteristics. First, a name can be found for it. Second, an actual fact can be found corresponding to it. Third, the name is not indeterminate with respect to the fact — that is, not indeterminate through confusion, nor indeterminate through impermanence. Fourth, the name applies to the fact without obstruction, consistently — never applying in one instance and failing in another.

items.zh: 現在相有者，謂若已生及因果性。如是一切，總說為一自相有法。
items.en: Existing in the mark of the present moment: it means whatever has already arisen, and stands in the relation of cause and effect. All of this together is called, as one, a thing existing by its own particular mark.

items.title: Shared-Mark Existence: Five Ways Things Genuinely Have Something in Common

items.zh: 何等名為共相有法？當知此相復有五種。一、種類共相，二、成所作共相，三、一切行共相，四、一切有漏共相，五、一切法共相。種類共相者，謂色、受、想、行、識等各別種類，總名為一種類共相。
items.en: What is called a thing existing by a shared mark? Know that this mark again has five kinds: first, shared mark of kind; second, shared mark of what is accomplished by action; third, shared mark of all conditioned things; fourth, shared mark of all that is defiled; and fifth, shared mark of all things whatsoever. Shared mark of kind: form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, each its own distinct kind — together named, as one, the shared mark of kind.

items.zh: 成所作共相者：謂善有漏法於感愛果，由能成辦所作共相，說名共相。如善有漏法於感愛果，如是不善法於感非愛果，念住、正斷、神足、根、力、覺支、道支菩提分法於得菩提，由能成辦所作共相，說名共相，當知亦爾。
items.en: Shared mark of what is accomplished by action: wholesome but still-defiled phenomena, in bringing about a desirable result, do so by a shared capacity to accomplish that result — this shared capacity is called the shared mark. Just as wholesome but still-defiled phenomena do this in bringing about a desirable result, so too unwholesome phenomena do this in bringing about an undesirable result, and the factors of enlightenment — the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of supernormal power, the faculties, the powers, the limbs of enlightenment, and the limbs of the path — do this in bringing about awakening: know that this too is a shared mark of what is accomplished by action.

items.zh: 一切行共相者，謂一切行無常性相。一切有漏共相者，謂有漏行者皆苦性相。一切法共相者，謂一切法空、無我性相。如是一切，總說為一共相有法。
items.en: Shared mark of all conditioned things: the nature of impermanence shared by every conditioned thing. Shared mark of all that is defiled: the nature of suffering shared by everything still defiled. Shared mark of all things whatsoever: the nature of emptiness and non-self shared by absolutely everything, conditioned and unconditioned alike. All of this together is called, as one, a thing existing by a shared mark.

blocks.text: Fascicle 16 begins the eleventh stage, the **Stage Attained Through Reflection** (思所成地), which runs through fascicle 19. Having heard the teaching, the practitioner now reflects on it: sorts what exists from what does not, and thinks through the scriptures. It is presented in three aspects: purity of self-nature, reflection on what is to be known, and reflection on the teachings. Today: the first, and the start of the second.

Reflection is pure when it has nine marks: reflecting alone, in a quiet place; avoiding what should not be contemplated (Master Cháng Bǎi: wrong thinking increases affliction or wastes time); distinguishing provisional from definitive teaching; relying on meaning rather than words; and carrying reflection to completion. The last brings "patience" (忍), which Venerable Miào Jìng explains as **certainty**: "before one couldn't be sure; now, through reflection, one is sure that all phenomena lack self."

subs.head: Reflecting on what is to be known

blocks.text: Reflection sorts things into what exists and what does not. Venerable Miào Jìng: 擇 is "picking and sorting". What exists is of five kinds: by its own mark, by a shared mark, merely designated, as cause, and as result.
**Existence by own mark** (自相有) has three kinds:

items: **ultimate** (勝義相有): the domain of transcendent wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seven suchnesses, within the perfected nature (Day 101);
**by observable features** (相狀相有): what can be named, cognised, and is not confused. Venerable Miào Jìng's example of confusion: to a sick person, bitter coptis tastes sweet;

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng's image for the contrast between existing and merely designated: the rope and the snake (Introduction 1). "The snake is empty of own mark; there is no snake at all; the rope is what exists."

**Shared-mark existence** (共相有) has five kinds: the shared mark of a kind, of what is accomplished, of all conditioned things (impermanence), of all contaminated things (suffering), and of all things (emptiness and non-self). Venerable Miào Jìng: a shared mark "doesn't exist by itself; only when many dharmas are together is it present."

On impermanence: a mountain looks still, but "like a person it moves forward day after day". On suffering: "those with affliction cling; this clinging is the cause of suffering." Master Cháng Bǎi distinguishes the last pair: emptiness stresses the absence of a real essence; non-self, the absence of a controlling agent.
Reflection, then, is not vague contemplation. It is careful sorting: this exists in this way; that is only a name.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by which three aspects is the Ground of Reflection briefly presented?
options: purity of self-nature, reflecting on what is cognized, reflecting on the teachings
quiz.why: "First, by way of purity of self-nature; second, by way of reflecting on what is cognized; and third, by way of reflecting on the teachings." Master Cháng Bǎi: the settled wisdom gained by proper reflection is the Ground of Reflection.

quiz.q: The second mark is avoiding what should not be contemplated. Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: wrong contemplation adds affliction or wastes time; right contemplation accords with the Dharma and leads to cultivated wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: some objects should be contemplated and some not; wrong thinking increases affliction or wastes time; right thinking accords with the Dharma and gives rise to wisdom from cultivation.

quiz.q: The ninth mark is carrying reflection to completion. What does the "patience" attained then mean, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: certainty — what was uncertain before, after reflection one is sure that all phenomena lack self
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Before there was no 忍; 忍 means certainty. Before one couldn't be sure; now, through reflection, one holds that phenomena lack self and is certain." The note's "new insight" misses this.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 擇 in 思擇所知?
options: discernment, i.e., observation — in plain words, picking and sorting
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "擇 is discernment — observing; in plain words, picking and choosing." The object examined is knowing what exists as having a mark and what doesn't as having none.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use to contrast existence by own mark with what is merely named?
options: rope and snake — the snake is empty of own mark, nonexistent; the rope truly exists by own mark
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The snake is empty of own mark — there is no snake at all; the rope is what exists — the rope exists by own mark." Ultimate existence isn't built from false conceptual names.

quiz.q: The note says shared-mark existence is "exactly as real" as own-mark existence. How does Venerable Miào Jìng define it?
options: it doesn't exist by itself; it exists only when many dharmas are together
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "It doesn't exist by itself; only when many dharmas are together is it present." Kind-sharing concerns results already gained; accomplishment-sharing, present action. The note says the opposite.

quiz.q: The shared mark of all things is emptiness and non-self. How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish the two?
options: emptiness stresses no real essence; non-self stresses no controlling function — though they are near-synonyms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Emptiness stresses lacking a real essence; non-self stresses lacking a controlling function — yet emptiness can also be called a synonym of non-self." Venerable Miào Jìng: both conditioned and unconditioned are empty.
